intelligence.bindingDescription: Disabled by default; available only when the credential agent is enabled. Match assets and credentials against captured traffic, link real requests or responses, and save matching excerpts. This does not attempt login or treat matching traffic as successful verification. Disabling the agent also disables linking; existing links are retained.
intelligence.agentDescription: Disabled by default. Independently process existing and new credentials, separating and highlighting usernames, passwords, tokens, and cookies without changing original reports or verification status. Complex text uses additional model tokens; parseable JSON does not require a model. Enable automatic recording first. Configure the model under Agents → Credential processing.
intelligence.recordDescription: Disabled by default. Reporting credentials, leads, and sensitive data increases task agent prompt and reporting token usage. This records data without starting credential processing. Disabling also turns off the agent and traffic linking below; existing intelligence and processed results remain available.

experimental.description:
Experimental mechanisms are disabled by default. They may change agent behavior or affect stability; enable them only after understanding the impact.

noa context compaction lets the model compact long conversation histories (norma v0.4.0). The four agent types (planner / worker / main agent / chat) use noa instead of built-in compaction. Original content is archived in the task workspace for review. Changes apply to subsequent runs without rebuilding agents; disabling restores built-in compaction immediately.

proxy.customProbeDescription: The service must return a plain-text IP or JSON in the format '{"ip":"1.2.3.4"}'. If public services are unreachable, or the host and internal proxy share a public IP, use an internal IP probe service. Different IPs for ① and ② confirm that traffic uses the internal proxy.

proxy.description:
All agent target traffic exits through this proxy to hide the source IP or use a relay. Supports http / https / socks5 with optional user:pass authentication. Leave blank for direct connections.

With traffic capture enabled, this is the recording proxy's upstream: traffic is stored before being forwarded. Without capture, it is injected directly into agent bash / WebFetch connections. It is independent of web search and LLM proxies.

Tip: with capture disabled, socks5 depends on each command-line tool supporting ALL_PROXY. curl works, but tools such as Python urllib fail. For socks5, enabling traffic capture is recommended: the MITM proxy handles the connection directly, transparently to tools.

binding.description:
Disabled by default. When enabled, the report agent triggered by a saved finding reviews existing HTTP requests/responses and links matching traffic before writing the report. Reviewing packets and additional tool calls increase token usage.

TCP findings and findings without captured or matching traffic can still be reported. This does not change traffic capture, manual linking, or access to saved evidence. It applies on the next agent turn; disabling immediately rejects new automatic links.

traffic.description:
When enabled, all agent HTTP traffic is stored through the recording proxy. Agents receive traffic_search / traffic_get tools and proxy configuration, including proxy instructions in their prompts.

When disabled (the default), no traffic is recorded. Agents do not receive proxy configuration or traffic tools, and their prompts exclude proxy instructions. Switching immediately rebuilds agents to apply the change.

pool.desc: When on, agents that don't specify a model automatically switch to the next profile whenever the current one is unusable (insufficient balance / expired key / rate limit / service error).

enable.hint: Off by default. When off, only the active profile is used and failures remain failures.

pool.note: The active profile is always first; others follow descending priority set in each profile. Failed profiles cool down (60s → 5min → 30min) and are skipped, then automatically rejoin. Profiles with insufficient context windows are skipped. Agents and tasks with specified models do not rotate by default.

For gateways using session headers for prompt caching or sticky routing. Stable across turns within a session and distinct across sessions. Blank disables it.

exclude.label: Excluded from rotation
exclude.hint: When enabled, this profile is excluded from failover but can still be explicitly selected by Agents or tasks. Useful for expensive profiles reserved for a particular Agent.

streaming.label: Streaming output
streaming.hint: When on (default), it runs over streaming SSE so you can watch real-time progress and live token counts during a run. When off, it runs truly non-streaming (stream:false, returning the full response at once), which can work around broken SSE implementations on some gateways (empty frames / frames missing the thinking field) but loses real-time progress during a run.

maxTokens.label: Output limit · Max tokens
maxTokens.hint: The maximum number of tokens to generate in a single response, sent with every request. 0 (default) = don't send this field and follow the server default. This differs from the "Context window" above, which is the model's total capacity and is used only to compute the compaction threshold locally. Set it too small and a reasoning model gets cut off during the thinking stage and can't answer a single character.

maxTokensFieldHint.openai: Which key to send the cap under. max_tokens is the default and most compatible gateways recognize only this. OpenAI's official reasoning models (the o-series / GPT-5), on the other hand, recognize only max_completion_tokens and throw an unsupported_parameter error the moment they receive max_tokens.
maxTokensFieldHint.anthropic: Only selectable for OpenAI format. Anthropic always uses max_tokens.
maxTokensFieldHint.openai-responses: Only selectable for OpenAI format. Responses API always uses max_output_tokens.

connect.title: Connection retries
connect.trigger: Connection failures or no HTTP 200 yet: connection reset, read/write timeout, DNS failures, other network errors, and HTTP 408, 429, 500, 502, 503, 504.
connect.skips: Other status codes (400 / 401 / 403 / 404 / 413 / 422, etc.) are deterministic rejections. Retrying would fail again, so they are propagated immediately.
connect.desc: Resends the same request unchanged. Once the stream starts (HTTP 200 received), interruptions are handled by another layer.

empty.title: Empty-response retries
empty.trigger: HTTP 200 with normal stop finish_reason but no content blocks at all. Empty gateway frames, missing reasoning fields, and sampling glitches can cause this.
empty.skips: Excludes empty content caused by max_tokens truncation. Increase the output limit instead; resending would hit the same limit.
empty.desc: Resends the entire prompt, which is expensive for long contexts. Keep the count low.

stream.title: Same-provider safe-window retries
stream.trigger: Failures after the stream is established (HTTP 200), such as disconnects, provider overload, or in-stream 429/5xx errors, before any token is delivered to the caller.
stream.skips: No retry for exhausted quota (402 / insufficient_quota, handled by profile rotation), long context (413 / context length, handled by compression), or deterministic 400 / 401 / 403 / 404 / 422 rejections.
stream.desc: Replays the same request on the same profile. Since no output was delivered, replay does not duplicate model output or tool execution.
stream.offHint: -1 = pass stream failures to the outer intent rerun layer

breaker.title: Rotation circuit breaker
breaker.trigger: Transient failures (429, 5xx, network errors) trip the circuit after consecutive failures reach the threshold. Deterministic failures such as insufficient balance (402), invalid keys (401/403), or missing models (404) trip it immediately.
breaker.skips: A single success resets the count, so intermittent failures do not slowly accumulate toward a trip.
breaker.desc: A tripped profile enters cooldown and is skipped by rotation. State is persisted across restarts.
breaker.offHint: -1 = never trip on transient failures (deterministic failures still trip)

intent.title: Intent reruns
intent.trigger: When earlier layers cannot recover, a Worker ends with model_error: inner retries exhausted, or the stream failed after output delivery began, when replay is unsafe and the whole intent must restart.
intent.skips: Quota exhaustion is handled by profile rotation, not reruns here. Paused, terminated, or wrapping-up tasks yield immediately without waiting through backoff.
intent.desc: Reruns the whole intent from the beginning. This is the outermost layer, so each rerun multiplies the attempts of all inner layers.
intent.offHint: -1 = no reruns; mark the intent blocked immediately

retry.emptyLine: Leave empty to use the default. {hint}.

override.label: Retry overrides
override.hint: Applies to this profile only, overriding the global defaults in "Retry & backoff." Leave a field empty to follow the global value. Enter -1 for the count to turn off this layer's retries. Fill in an interval to use a fixed interval instead of exponential backoff. The circuit breaker and intent re-run are per process, so they can be adjusted only on the global page.

retry.intro: A single model-call failure passes through five retry layers in order from innermost to outermost: <chain>connection → empty response → same-provider safe window → rotation circuit breaker → intent re-run</chain>. An outer layer's turn comes only after the inner one is used up, so the counts <emph>multiply together</emph>. Max out every layer and a single hiccup can burn dozens of requests. Leaving them all empty is the current default, exactly the behavior when this page didn't exist. The first three layers can be overridden individually on each model profile.
